memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'The priest is to take from her hands the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the Lord and bring it to the altar. The priest is then to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial offering and burn it on the altar; after that, he is to have the woman drink the water. If she has made herself impure and been unfaithful to her husband, then when she is made to drink the water that brings a curse, it will go into her and cause bitter suffering; her abdomen will swell and her womb will miscarry, and she will become a curse. If, however, the woman has not made herself impure, but is clean, she will be cleared of guilt and will be able to have children.' - Num 5:25-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There are two possible outcomes to this solemn test, and it is worth noticing the second one carefully. If the woman was innocent, she "will be cleared of guilt." Her name would be restored, her innocence established by God Himself, and she would be free to live without a cloud of suspicion hanging over her.

This is easily overlooked, but it mattered enormously. In a culture where a woman had almost no way to defend herself against a jealous husband's accusation, this procedure gave the innocent woman something precious: public vindication from God. No more whispers, no more suspicion. God Himself had declared her clean.

There is a beautiful truth here about God's character. He is a God who clears the innocent and vindicates those who have been wrongly suspected. He does not leave His people forever under a cloud of false accusation.

This points us to a greater vindication. In Christ, all who trust Him are declared clean — not because we passed a test, but because He passed it for us. God "justifies" us, which means He declares us cleared, right in His sight (Rom 8:1, 33). There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

If you belong to Jesus, hear this today: in God's sight, you stand cleared. The accusations that would condemn you have no power, because Christ has made you clean.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does it comfort you that God vindicates the innocent?
- What does it mean that in Christ you are declared "clean"?
- How can you rest in "no condemnation" today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ I am cleared and declared clean. Help me to rest in Your verdict rather than under the weight of accusation. Amen.
